sections.h2: What should I know first about selling a house in Portage, Michigan?
sections.html:
Portage sellers deal with three offices: the city for permits and property tax bills, the Kalamazoo County Register of Deeds for the deed, and the county treasurer for the tax certificate that has to be on a warranty deed. A sale to a cash buyer, a listing with an agent and a sale to a neighbor all run through those same three desks.

Portage sits in Kalamazoo County and is the smaller of the two main cities in the Kalamazoo-Portage metro area. The area was settled in 1830 and Portage became a city in 1963. Several things set it apart from a typical Michigan suburb: two lakes in the southeast corner, a very large pharmaceutical plant, and a tornado in May 2024 that cut across town from one side to the other.

The sections below cover the local facts that matter when you price, prepare and close on a house here.

sections.h2: How large is Portage and what do the Census figures show?
sections.html:
Portage covers 32.29 square miles of land, which makes it a spread-out city with a density of about 1,514 people per square mile. The Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 49,862 residents, up 2.0 percent from the 2020 base of 48,882.

sections.h2: Which Portage landmarks and neighborhoods do buyers ask about?
sections.html:
Buyers who search Portage often start with the water. Austin Lake lies in the southeast part of the city, named for a settler who arrived from New York in 1833, and West Lake sits right beside it with Portage Road running between the two. Houses on or near the lakes are a separate segment from the subdivisions farther north and west.

School district is the other common question, because the city is split. Most of Portage belongs to Portage Public Schools, while smaller areas fall in Comstock Public Schools, Vicksburg Community Schools and Schoolcraft Community Schools. Put the district name in your listing or tell your buyer outright, since a parcel's district follows the district boundary and not the city name on the mailing address.

Commutes are short. The Census Bureau reports a mean of 19.7 minutes to work, and the city's two large employers explain much of that local pull:

  • Pfizer runs its largest manufacturing facility in Portage, on about 1,300 acres.
  • Stryker has been headquartered in Portage since 2023 and operates several manufacturing sites in the city.
  • Kalamazoo, the larger of the two main cities in the metro area, supplies much of the rest of the job base.

sections.h2: What did the May 2024 tornado change for Portage sellers?
sections.html:
The tornado that struck Portage on May 7, 2024 was rated high-end EF2, and reports after the storm counted more than 500 damaged buildings, 60 of them destroyed. The city set up a tornado recovery page for residents and businesses, and the damage path is still the first thing some out-of-town buyers ask about.

If your house was repaired after the storm, gather the permits, contractor invoices and any insurance paperwork into one folder. A buyer who pays cash will still want to know which roof, siding or windows are new. If the house is unrepaired, say so up front and consider whether an as-is sale makes more sense than a repair project. Permits for construction work go through the Portage Department of Community Development, and the Treasury Office collects the permit fees.

The city's recovery page also lists nonprofit disaster case management for people affected by the storm, which can help with insurance and housing questions while you decide whether to sell. Ask the city manager's office for current contacts, since program details change over time.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed in Kalamazoo County?
sections.html:
The Kalamazoo County Register of Deeds charges $30.00 per document to record a deed, and it adds $3.00 for each extra instrument a document assigns or discharges. The office takes cash, check, money order, debit and credit card, and recording checks go to the Kalamazoo County Register of Deeds.

Warranty deeds, deeds with covenant warranty, land contracts and master deeds need a tax certificate from the county treasurer before recording. The fee is $5.00 for up to 20 tax ID numbers per document and $0.20 for each further description. The extra $10.00 city certificate on the same page applies to parcels inside the City of Kalamazoo, so a Portage parcel does not need it.

Transfer tax follows the sale price on the deed, rounded up to the next $500 step. The county's printed rates are $1.10 per thousand dollars for the county and $7.50 per thousand dollars for the state. Under MCL 207.523 the seller is liable for the tax, so build it into your net sheet and ask the title company for the exact figure.

sections.h2: When are Portage property taxes due and what happens at closing?
sections.html:
Portage bills summer taxes due September 14 and winter taxes due February 14, and both bills cover January 1 through December 31 of the tax year. Summer bills are payable from August 1 and winter bills from December 1, and a due date that falls on a weekend moves to the following Monday.

  • Real property taxes still unpaid on March 1 of the next year go to the Kalamazoo County Treasury, which adds its own interest and penalties.
  • Special assessments for water, sewer and city street work are billed in July with an August 31 due date, so check for an open installment on the parcel.
  • A mortgage company or escrow agent can ask the city for a copy of the tax listing once the original bills are mailed.

For a rough view of the buyer's bill, the city points to the State of Michigan Property Tax Estimator, where future owners enter the state equalized value and current owners enter the taxable value. The Portage assessor's office also has a property record form that corrects square footage, bedroom counts and similar facts. Fix any errors before a buyer's appraiser pulls the record.

sections.h2: Can I sell a Portage house that has tenants?
sections.html:
Yes. A rented house can sell with the tenant in place or empty, and the lease and your notice rights decide the timing.

Since late 2025 the city has also run a rental listing website for landlords, with free listings for owners of fewer than 20 units. If you want a quicker route than finding a new tenant, a buyer who plans to keep renting may accept the lease as it is. Ask the city's Community Development office which local rules apply to your rental, and bring the current lease to every showing.

faqs.q: How much does Kalamazoo County charge to record a deed from a Portage sale?
faqs.a: The recording fee is $30.00 per document. A warranty deed also needs a county treasurer tax certificate at $5.00 for up to 20 tax ID numbers, so budget for both.

faqs.q: Who pays the transfer tax when a Portage house sells?
faqs.a: The seller. MCL 207.523 makes the seller or grantor liable, and the county prints rates of $1.10 and $7.50 per thousand dollars of the sale price on its fee schedule.

faqs.q: When are the two Portage tax bills due?
faqs.a: Summer taxes are due September 14 and winter taxes February 14, moved to Monday when the date lands on a weekend. Anything unpaid on March 1 goes to the county treasury.

faqs.q: Do tornado-damaged Portage houses sell as is?
faqs.a: They can. The May 7, 2024 tornado damaged more than 500 buildings, and an unrepaired house simply sells at a price that reflects the work. Keep permits and insurance records handy for repaired houses.

faqs.q: Which school district is my Portage house in?
faqs.a: Most of the city is in Portage Public Schools, and smaller areas are in Comstock, Vicksburg or Schoolcraft. Check the parcel with the district or the city assessor before you list.
